item.title: Mahabharat (Hindi Anuwad Sahit)
item.description:
Author: Ved Vyas

(आदिपर्व)

नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् ⁠। देवीं सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्

उग्रश्रवा सौति

जनमेजयके

निष्प्रभेऽस्मिन् निरालोके सर्वतस्तमसावृते ⁠। बृहदण्डमभूदेकं प्रजानां बीजमव्ययम् ⁠।⁠।⁠ २९ ⁠।⁠।

यदिदं दृश्यते किंचिद् भूतं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ⁠। पुनः संक्षिप्यते सर्वं जगत् प्राप्ते युगक्षये ⁠।⁠।⁠ ३८ ⁠।⁠। यह जो कुछ भी स्थावर-जंगम जगत् दृष्टिगोचर होता है, वह सब प्रलयकाल आनेपर अपने कारणमें विलीन हो जाता है ⁠।⁠।⁠ ३८ ⁠।⁠।

१- ग्रन्थका उपक्रम, ग्रन्थमें कहे हुए अधिकांश विषयोंकी संक्षिप्त सूची तथा इसके पाठकी महिमा

जो विद्वान् ब्राह्मण अकेला ही दस सहस्र जिज्ञासु व्यक्तियोंका अन्न-दानादिके द्वाराराभरण-पोषण करता है, उसे कुलपति कहते हैं।

item.title: The Mythology Book
item.description:
• Greek word “muthos” meaning story and “logia” meaning Knowledge
  • Except the Pirahas: an Amazonian Tribe, every human culture comes up with its mythology to explain its origin.
  • Mesopotamian civilization started living in cities and Sumerians developed their first pantheon of deities.
    • Stories like Epic of Gilgamesh, statues, and carvings.
  • In Greece, almost 1000 cities had their own sets of founding myths, which led to contradiction among one another. Poets like Homer and Hesiod created a comprehensive Greek mythology from their writings. Homer through Iliad and Odyssey, while Hesiod Hesiod’s Theogony.
  • IN 600 bc, anonymous wrote tribute to 33 gods.
  • Mycenae, described by Homer as city rich in gold, was founded in 1600 BCE.
  • Classical era in Greece began with the fall of powerful Persian Empire in 479 BCE. After defeating Persians, city states of Athens and Sparta fought over control of Greece. Athens set a lot of myths because of it being a pre-eminent power.
  • Athenian dominance ended in 4th century BCE when Alexander the Great built his empire. He is responsible for exporting Greek culture and mythology all the way up to India.

Highlights

The word “mythology” comes from the Greek muthos, meaning “story” and logia, “knowledge

item.title: Rig Veda
item.description:
1. Rig Veda is the oldest existing text in any Indo-European language.

Rig Veda was composed around 1700 BC with the oldest parts as early as 2000 BC. There is still no fixed time when it was first composed. The time expressed is based on the events that are described in this book.

  1. Rig Veda is the world’s oldest religious text in continuous use. 4000 years of unbroken tradition is something worth venerable.

  2. The Rig Veda was not written down until about 500 AD.

  • loc 3818 - The exercise, dubbed “Eligible Receiver,” pitted a red team of NSA hackers against the networks of the US Pacific Command in Hawaii. The team was prohibited from using inside knowledge to conduct the attack or anything but off-the-shelf tools that were available to ordinary hackers. When the attack began, they launched their offensive through a commercial dial-up internet account and barreled straight into the military’s networks with little resistance. The system administrators in Hawaii, who had no advance knowledge of the exercise, spotted only two of the multiple intrusions the attackers made over the course of ninety days, but even then they thought nothing of the breaches because they resembled the kind of ordinary traffic that administrators expected to see on the network. It wasn’t unlike the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941, when an alert operator at the Opana Radar Site on the island of Oahu spotted inbound aircraft heading toward the island but didn’t raise an alarm because his superiors believed they were friendlies. The red-team hackers dropped marker files onto the systems to plant a virtual flag, proving they were there, and also created a number of simulated attacks showing how they could have seized control of power and communications networks in Oahu, Los Angeles, Chicago, and Washington, DC. It was that fear-driven, obsequious journalism that led the Times, the Post, and many other outlets to refuse to use the word “torture” in their reporting on Bush interrogation techniques, even though they freely used that word to describe the exact same tactics when used by other governments around the world. It was also what produced the debacle of media outlets laundering baseless government claims about Saddam and Iraq to sell the American public on a war built of false pretenses that the US media amplified rather than investigated. Yet another unwritten rule designed to protect the government is that media outlets publish only a few such secret documents, and then stop.
